This is basically photoshop but for sprites. Truly a fantastic piece of software with a good price point. I've used it for both simple and quick things, and longer, more complex things. I really enjoy using it, and will continue to enjoy using it!
i enjoy using this to mod games, and its very impresive with all the neat features

recently started, and i cant believe how easy is to use and you constantly learn new stuff .

10/10 in full price. Absolutely GOD if in sale.
I use this all the time to make art, Great Pixel Program for beginners all the way to experts! Grab it if you wanna try Pixel Art

I know most people looking for pixelart-programs has already found this one, but if this review somehow helps anyone that hasn't already made the decision to grab Aseprite, do yourself a favor and don't hold it off any longer.

Fantastic program.

Pretty fantastic piece of software. I've been using it for years, and recently got my free steam key.

The toolset works really well out of the box as a simple pixel art editor.

There is no problem using Aseprite to make the pixel art UI & characters for Unity, Monogame/XNA, LibGDX, ImpactJS, or RPGmaker/GameMaker/Construct. The export feature works great as well.

Anyone who wants to get started with pixel art and wants an easy to use editor designed for it from the ground up, should get this.

My favourite software to make pixel art with. I used to use the Windows XP version of MsPaint for ages, but Aseprite was so intuitive that it wasn't a hard switch to make.

There's a handful of things that I hope Aseprite will add at some point (such as layer masks) and some strange behaviour in relation to having to deselect a selection when you move selected areas simultaneously with multiple layers affected before the movement gets applied to every layer, but all in all it's still great software that you can't really go wrong with.
I've been learning pixel art with aseprite for a week now and it's simply perfect. Everything is just so intuitive. It's also perfectly stable on Linux!

This software is an amazing pixel art software, super easy to use, the UI is very pleasant and it makes animating pixels and drawing pixels super easy. Would absolutely suggest purchasing this game if you can.

This is, in every way, a preliminary recommendation. I've spent a short amount of time going through the tools and capabilities and Aseprite fits the bill that no other program I've used ever has, in my opinion.

It's perfectly suited for the task at hand. It's easy to use, and exactly what I've been looking for. A capable pixel art editor with the exact features needed to create sprites, tilesets, background, all animated... with none of the extra clutter.

I am very eager to see if it integrates & plays well with Sprite Lamp, a program I held off on purchasing until I found the "right" software for me.

I highly recommend Aseprite, will be utilizing it for a long time to come.

NOTE: I have spent perhaps 4 hours with it, via "non-steam" launching. Which is handy, if you are running a steam program minimized/in the tray.. or working concurrently with a steam-based copy of Godot, GMS2, RPGmaker etc..

Simply amazing. This is like a very specialized version of Photoshop, just for Pixel Art. Nearly all of the controls and hotkeys are exactly the same as are the functions. If you know even a little about using Photoshop then you'll be right at home with this. So far in my experience it's been very stable, it's had every feature that I've needed so far and all of this for a simply amazing price. I can't recommend it highly enough. I purchased this through Humble Bundle so I could have keys for Steam and the DRM free version, I'd recommend anyone else to do the game.

This is a very good program.
It has a simple interface for any workflow, or hobbies, and it has simple tools available for most things.
At first glance it seems limited, but with experience many hidden gems are discovered that make it further useful and fun to use.

Aseprite is the best pixel art tool in the market.

Here is what made it great for me:
- Easy layer workout.
- Compatible and smooth with my Wacom Intuos Pro.
- Amazing palette control and conformity. (Being able to change between systems is a gem.)
- Easy to add and track frames for animation.
- Easy spritesheet.
- Very light load on cpu and memory.
- No unnecessary gimmicks outside of pixel art.
- Great and easy to learn UI.

This is a TOP and MUST HAVE software for all pixel artists.

It's a really good pixel software, probably the one that i like the most. The UI is pretty intuitive, and things are pretty straightforward!
If you decide and have the chance to support this, totally go for it

This piece of software has become my absolute favourite art program to work in, not just for sprites, but in general. It is incredibly intuitive to use and just a lot of fun to work with.

I am especially fond of the contour tool. It makes blocking out shapes extremely easy. Also, the dithering gradient options are amazing for someone who was already obsessed with halftones/screentones like myself.
I love this software. Creating bit art in this feels like a creative artistic puzzle video game. lol

Although confusing at first, Aseprite is a simplistic software that allows you to be creative and get the job done without overly fanciness. Coming from Spriting in Photoshop, it has limitations, but also excels so easily at things like animations. I use it for personal projects and school work primarily. Highly recommend.

Aseprite is quite good.
It's got everything you would really want for pixel art, the tiling tools are great. It makes making pixel art fun.

All the controls are intuitive, choosing to follow a similar layout to Photoshop instead of reinventing the wheel, which I really appreciate because it makes it easy to pick up.

Well worth the price.

I've always been in awe of pixelart and having discovered this tool finally gave me the confidence to get started on some myself, Aseprite is an amazing tool for Pixelart and Animations alike, it's simple and straight forward with lots of extra bits and pieces to make drawing as smooth and satisfying as possible. Highly recommend it to even beginner artist such as myself~!

I started using Aseprite after using Paint.net for a good few years. Overall it does definitely leave a little bit to be desired from Paint.net, though honestly after using Aseprite for a few hours most of those desires are completely forgotten. And either way, the few inconveniences are without a doubt outweighed by the many many pros.

I've been working with pixel art for a little over a year (or maybe two) now, and I was originally in love with GraphicsGale, a free PC application, after exploring a ton of other options. While I still use it for some things (mainly it's text tool for some of the stuff I do) I've pretty much moved exclusively to Aseprite. The way animations are displayed in the timeline is beautiful and flexible; the main reason I made the switch in the first place. For anybody working on complex sprite animations this is the way to go.
Love it, so much. I can not recommend this enough for pixel art and creating game sprites.

It took 6,990 hours but I managed to complete one project before starting ten new ones. Hands down my favorite art program. Easy to learn but endless functionality, rarely do I feel like I lack a tool for the situation. Runs great on even the most basic of computers so I can use it on my cheap laptop while I'm away from home. Only downside is my friends always see me playing it and ask if I can show them my art, so I have to actually go back and finish some of my art projects.

For me personally, this is by far the best pixel art software you can find out there.

It's simple enough for any beginner, but also so darn in-depth that any experienced scripter/pixel-artist will be at peace here. The devs care intensely about this software and are really open about any development-thoughts on their twitter or discord. The community around it also is just pure gold.

If you are just even remotely interested in trying pixel-art, this is the way to go! 100%

This is the gold standard for pixel art in current year. One of the most worthwhile purchases you could make if you ever want to make pixel art. Much better than trying to do it in Photoshop or whatever people do.
Easy to use and powerful for its intended purpose. It doesn't have an insane amount of features, but it does exactly what you need it to do for the creation of 2D frame-based animations.

For someone who was using Piskel at first when I started making pixel art, and then pixel animation, this is sooo nice to move to. I really like the pixel perfect feature, I like how easy it is to manipulate the sizing of things, and generally what I could imagine to want in a pixel making program, it has(haven't found anything I couldn't do). Whether you make pixel art for fun, for personal products, or for commissions, I would say it's worth it.

EDIT: People have been asking the devs to add dither brushes since 2014 and they still haven't done it. And no, the cumbersome custom brushes aren't an actual solution.

My pixel art program of choice for the past four years or so. It has some nice pixel art specific features that Photoshop and the like don't have, such as pixel perfect strokes (pixels won't double up while free hand drawing), resolution independent reference layers, RotSprite rotation, and more.

One thing I wish I had know sooner is that it does in fact have a text tool. It doesn't appear on the toolbar, you press T to use it.

Cannot recommend this enough; one of the most GOATed graphic design softwares in existence. There's so much value there you have no idea. Get this already if you are going to work with pixels and animations of the such. Even for general doodling, this is fantastic. 9999/10

I'm not an artist and but can use photoshop, gimp, inkscape to an average level. This product is amazing for pixel art. It makes animations simple. You can merge layers. You have onion skins so you can see forward and backward on frames. And one of my favorite parts is the tile map where you can actually build your level's look and feel. (TBH, I'm not sure if you can show animations on the tile map yet.)

Coolness
* Onion Skin for animation smoothing
* Layers (lockable, movable)
* Nice grid control
* Animation Player
* Tile maps with output
* Tile maps change one or all like tiles, very cool
* Mirroring by vertical or horizontal or both
* Expected tools: Magic wand, fill, fill shape, etc
* Palette loader
* Good recovery system
* Good tab system so you can work on 10+ pieces
* Nice grid system

Of course there are a few clunky things but this just comes with learning the program. The picker doesn't get alpha unless you set something. Dragging layers involves dragging the yellow box not the layer. Linking cells doesn't quite make sense to me yet. To create a large tile map you need to create a large sprite first, this was a bit confusing. Expanding the palette is a bit tricky. Manually selecting tiles to change, cut, or replicate took me to learn which settings.

Anyway, great product even to just tinker with. Thank you.

AMAZING.. I WILL POST A BETTER REVIEW AFTER USING THIS MORE EXTENSIVELY BUT YOU CAN DL ENTIRE VERSION TO TRY FOR FREE, YOU JUST CAN'T SAVE FILES UNTIL YOU BUY. GO TO: ASEPRITE.ORG . Absolutely incredible, i can't believe the price.

Fantastic piece of Pixel software and a must have for any enthusiast or indie dev looking to make some art for their game. 

Plugin support (check itch for anything you might need)
Plenty of tools (doesn't feel like the emblem editor from Mario Kart DS)
Exporting is easy with different options and file types supported
Good animation tools
Ability to import or create your own colour palette

Truly the Deluxe Paint of the modern age. Though I've not seen anyone re-create King Tut's death mask yet

11/10, would pay for it again if I could. Only complaint is that there's no support for workshop. it'd be a nice addition but not vital
Its basically MS paint, but 1000 times better and made with pixel art in mind. If that alone doesnt sell this to you I dont know what will
A great tool for making pixel artwork, whether it be for a game or just for the fun of it.

Tried to start pixel art with a few different apps multiple times and failed hard.

Aseprite really makes it fun to learn the art. Easy to use, pretty self explanatory and smooth running workflows.

It's good. Like for real. Perfect for pixel art pictures and animation.
Best tool for drawing pixel art. No subscriptions, no bullshit. Buy once, use it for a lifetime.

Excellent app for pixel art, static or animated, if you do pixel artwork as hobbyist or professional, just buy it!

+PRO: Very easy to use and also a lot low weight in memory compared with Photoshop and Gimp.
-CON: I think just need some extra art features, like some basic filters and more brushes.
its pretty much perfect. i cant find a feature that really needs improving. great value

200hrs in I can say its pretty dam good.

+Easy to animate with
+Easy to add new scripts
+Handy Tile and Mirror modes to speed things up
+Export option to turn animations into a single sprite sheet
+Some more stuff

A good and fair priced a software for newbie graphic designers. Creating tilemaps is easy and versatile. This is a great tool for creating pixel art but it misses a tile palette for testing the tiles. I would need another paid program for that.
Easy to use, great software to pass time and be creative. Money spent is definitely worth it.

If you're making a video game that's going to need a lot of pixel art you NEED this software. All of the tools, presets, palettes, and even PIXEL WIDTH AND HEIGHT make it easier and more enjoyable than ever to put together those squares.
Aseprite has helped me so much with game dev is so wonderful and worth the money.

For myself as an amateur game developer with little to no artistic skills, this app has been a life saver when it comes to making basic art and animation for my games. The interface is extremely clean and it has all the right tools to make pixel art and animation as much of a breeze as such things could be. I couldn't be happier with a 2D art and animation tool!
It is an incredible help in creating different animations and games, i am right now making a game out of it. :)
Great software for pixel art. I can sometimes feel some hiccups when using the app on Macbook compared to Desktop PC but overall the software is amazing

I really have to say I used gimp before but Asesprite offers some really great features for PixelArt for its price. You can import your own pallets as well as make super great curves. I am very satisfied with this program and will certainly continue to use it for my games :)

I've spent so much time in this app, so much. Even though it doesn't have the automation of programs like Photoshop and Krita I still come back to it time and time again because it's precise and has all of the tools I need as a RPGmaker Dev.

tldr.text: Overwhelmingly Positive (99%): players love the graphics and art, which 60% of reviews praise.
Complaints are few and spread across different topics, so none stands out.
